caption: Honestly: an ordinary (non-secure) view's detail page — a secure view looks identical here.

code:
CREATE OR REPLACE SECURE VIEW widgets_view AS
  SELECT w.*
  FROM widgets AS w
  WHERE w.id IN (
    SELECT widget_id
    FROM widget_access_rules AS a
    WHERE upper(role_name) = CURRENT_ROLE()
  );
caption: SECURE hides this WHERE clause and the table names it references from anyone without the privilege to see them.
IS_SECURE confirms status; SET/UNSET SECURE toggle it without recreating the view.

code:
-- A secure view's query is NOT exposed to the optimizer the same way a
-- regular view's is, which can mean fewer execution-plan optimizations
-- (e.g. predicate pushdown across the view boundary can be more limited).
-- Use SECURE only where that privacy guarantee is actually needed --
-- not as a default on every view.
caption: A real, documented trade-off — reach for SECURE where the privacy guarantee matters, not by default.
